items.title: Clarence "Little Dad" Vincent Interview, 1960-01-21
items.q: Me and him and Eddie Hickman. Three piece.

ctx.x: Ask him about Eddie Hickman. He asked him.

How's about Eddie Hickman? Eddie Hickman, well Eddie Hickman, he had a band. He had George McCullum, he had Artie Crasman, and he had Max Williams, and he had Little Lawrence, Little Lawrence Coleman, and Gitar, no, Gitar, yeah. He's dead too. I believe Eddie's dead too. I read in the paper last week if it's him, you know, Eddie Hickman, you know. It wasn't. I don't know. Oh, you don't know him, man. He's an old musician too. This shot fella, he wasn't much taller than me. He gets mad quick. He's a nice liquor…

items.title: Clarence "Little Dad" Vincent Interview, 1960-01-21
items.q: I used to play with him sometimes too. Me and him and Eddie Hickman. Three piece.

ctx.x: Yeah, I heard talk about him.

Oh, yeah. He used to play with people. And then he played with us. And then he played with George Williams, big George Williams. Then he had a band, you know. Boy, he played with Peerrell until Peerrell died. Then after that, he didn't spend with anybody, you know. Work all the time. He was a printer, you know. Played music at night. He was a heavy drinker. He was the finest man in one of me. He didn't look at him up there. I used to play with him sometimes too. Me and him and Eddie Hickman. Three piece. He could…

items.title: Clarence "Little Dad" Vincent Interview, 1959-12-11
items.q: Eddie Hickman, he was a bass player too. He used to play with the Alcorn brothers.

ctx.x: He's had a brother, Kenia, that's the one. He was a violin player in the Kish Sonson. He'd tell you to play with him three or four pieces. Like hustling and that, send a job down the district. He'd play like that. He'd look like happy, huh? So, um... Very happy. Very happy. Very happy. He died now. He died up in Chicago. He could play with me when I was playing with John Robeser.
